_comment: FROZEN issue codes: the exact `issues[].code` strings alp-sdk-vscode
matches with `===` to gate real behaviour. Every one of those matches
FAILS OPEN -- an unrecognised code is indistinguishable from 'no
problem', so a rename here is silent on both sides with CI green. See
alplabai/tan-cli#106.
This file is the single source. Python's shipping emit sites are checked
in both directions by `python/tests/gates/test_every_issue_code_is_registered.py`
and `test_frozen_issue_codes.py`; `crates/tan-cli/tests/contract.rs` owns
only entries whose `emittedBy` path points into the frozen Rust oracle.
The release workflow folds the combined registry into `envelope-contract.json`
asset so the extension's own contract test can diff against an artefact
instead of a hand-copied fixture.
Adding a `frozen` code is cheap. REMOVING or RENAMING one is a breaking
wire change: bump the CLI MAJOR/MINOR, say so in CHANGELOG.md, and open
the matching issue on alp-sdk-vscode. Do not 'fix' a rename by
loosening the consumer to a prefix match -- `bootstrap.` would swallow
codes it has no verdict for.
A `reserved` code is the pre-consumer state: the spelling exists at the
emission site (the gate still checks that) but `consumer` is "none" --
nobody matches it with `===` yet, so renaming or dropping it costs
nothing on the wire. Promote a `reserved` code to `frozen` the moment a
consumer binds to it (fill in `consumer`/`consumerEffect` for real); do
not invent a third status for that transition.
EVERY literal emit site must appear here at some status (tan-cli#219).
`frozen_issue_codes` only ever walked registry -> source, so a code that
was never registered was ungated on BOTH sides at once: this repo's
checks iterate the registry and never saw it, and alp-sdk-vscode's gate
keys off the published artefact, which is built from this same registry.
A rename of an unregistered code was invisible to both repos
simultaneously. `every_emitted_issue_code_is_registered` walks the other
way and fails when an emitted code has no entry. 41 codes were in that
state when it landed; they are `reserved`, NOT `frozen` -- freezing what
no consumer reads would over-commit and make every future internal
rename a contract break for nobody's benefit.
The published `envelope-contract.json` carries this array WHOLE, all
three statuses, not a frozen-only subset -- so the artefact's code list
is everything tan emits, and a consumer reads `status` to decide what a
code promises. Keep it that way: a silently-partial artefact that
presents itself as the contract is worse than either honest option.
`literal` (tan-cli#372): required on a `crates/` entry, where it is the
verbatim Rust needle `crates/tan-cli/tests/contract.rs` substring-checks
against source. A `python/` entry must NOT carry this field at all --
`test_frozen_issue_codes.py` (which owns every python-side entry, per
tan-cli#363) checks emission with an `ast` parse instead and never reads
it, so a value here would be mandatory-to-supply and verified by
nobody. It was: 42 of the 198 python-side entries had already gone stale
under that regime, unnoticed, before the field was dropped for that
whole side. `contract.rs::check_or_delegate` asserts the absence, so a
python-side entry cannot silently regain a value nothing will ever check.
SDK-root refusal naming (tan-cli#1463): a code for 'no usable alp-sdk
checkout' is spelled `<command>.sdk-root-unresolved`, the majority
spelling (build, model, generate, trace, validate, presets, pinmux,
examples, explain, init, bootstrap). New and reserved codes follow it.
The older `clean.sdk-root-not-found` and `flash.sdk-root-not-found`,
`init.sdk-root-invalid`, `kconfig.no-sdk-root` and `support-bundle.sdk-root`
are FROZEN or already registered and are NOT renamed: a rename is a
breaking wire change (see above). Such a refusal's message names where the
ladder looked via `tan.core.sdk_discovery.with_sdk_search` (flash and clean
call `sdk_search_summary` directly), unless an explicit `--sdk-root` was
rejected, which is terminal (I-31) and is named by
`rejected_sdk_root_message` instead.

A checkout whose bound schema file is simply absent emits nothing under THIS code -- as of tan-cli#964's review it emits `debug-config.metadata-schema-unchecked` instead (below), not silence; see `tan.core.metadata_schema.validate_document`. issue #1154: recorded via `Log.warn` in `_sdk_credential`, replacing the `Authenticating the Zephyr SDK download ...` line for that run. tan carries its GitHub credential to `west sdk install` out of band, in a private netrc pointed at by `$NETRC`, and that route rests on facts about code tan neither owns nor pins. What it rests on is NOT, as this note said until tan-cli#1170, west's no-token branch sending an empty header dict: measured on `requests` 2.34.2, the netrc lookup is gated on `self.trust_env and not auth and not self.auth` -- the `auth=` ARGUMENT, never the headers -- and `prepare_auth` runs after `prepare_headers`, so a netrc match OVERWRITES an `Authorization` header passed through `headers=` and a header suppresses nothing. The two shapes that DO leave tan's netrc unread are a `requests` call carrying its own `auth=` and a session built with `trust_env=False`. This fires when the resolved `<zephyr_base>/scripts/west_commands/sdk.py` no longer matches the shape that reasoning was measured against -- four substring facts: neither suppressing shape present; `args.personal_access_token` still present, so west's own token still arrives on that flag; `req_headers = {}` still present, which is what makes the flag's `else:` arm mean anything; and every environment variable the file reads inside `{ZEPHYR_BASE, ZEPHYR_SDK_INSTALL_DIR}` (measured at Zephyr v4.4.1 `scripts/west_commands/sdk.py:231`/`:473`/`:478`/`:573`, unchanged at v4.4.2 and on `zephyrproject/main` @8a4e180b93e). A TRIPWIRE, not a parser: a west that stops using `requests` altogether, or a partial move off `--personal-access-token` that leaves the attribute mentioned anywhere, satisfies all four, so the ABSENCE of this code is not proof the route is intact. The credential is still staged and still passed -- it may well still work -- but tan stops CLAIMING the download is authenticated, because an inert credential is worse than an absent one: it removes the symptom that would send the reader to find a token. Deliberately NOT a CI gate and deliberately NOT `WORKSPACE_BLOCKING`: `requests` is not a tan dependency and `ci.yml` checks out alp-sdk but never zephyr, so a CI-time check would skip everywhere, and an unauthenticated download usually still succeeds. Silent when the file cannot be read at all -- "could not look" is not evidence the assumption broke. Pre-consumer -- nothing in alp-sdk-vscode matches this code yet. Never carries the token value: the message names only the VARIABLE.

tan-cli#491 defect 4: the ONE envelope a `--format json` run interrupted by Ctrl-C reports. SIGINT does not reach `tan.cli.main` as a raw `KeyboardInterrupt` -- Typer catches it and re-raises `Exit(130)`, which Click turns into `sys.exit(130)` -- so before this code existed an interrupted run was indistinguishable from any other non-zero exit with no envelope and fell into the `cli.parse-error` fallback: an envelope asserting the COMMAND LINE was invalid for a run that was already programming a board, at an `exitCode` of 130, outside the contract's fixed 0-5 set. The envelope reports `exitCode` 1 (`ExitCode.RUNTIME_FAILURE`) and the process exits 1 to match, since the wire invariant is `process exit code == envelope.exitCode` (tan-cli#327); TEXT mode is untouched and still exits 130 through Click's own machinery. A DELIBERATE divergence from the frozen v0.4.1 oracle, which has no SIGINT handler at all and simply dies from the signal with zero bytes on stdout -- the port cannot copy that and still keep `stdout is the envelope channel`. issueCodes.consumerEffect: Warns that the implicit stdin dump was NOT read to a clean EOF -- one of the idle/byte-cap/total bounds fired first, and the decode proceeded on whatever arrived. A panel can surface this as a caveat on an otherwise-successful decode: the report is real, but a slower or larger producer may have had more to say. issueCodes.note: Exit 0 on the success path; also reachable alongside `faultdecode.no-registers` at exit 2 when a bound fires WITH bytes read but nothing in them parsed into a complete register set (constraint 4's hole, closed after initial review: a refusal used to announce nothing about the truncation it was itself caused by). Added by tan-cli#537, the implicit-stdin-reader redesign: seven prior attempts on tan-cli#503 each traded one defect (a dropped dump, an unbounded hang, unbounded memory growth, a decode-parity break, a truncation nobody was told about) for another, in the same function.
